title: Fix DST windowing in billing aggregation causing negative invoice adjustments
creator: Owen Patel
description: Several EU customers reported negative invoice line-items and unexplained credits after the clock changes for DST (spring forward / fall back). Investigation shows the hourly aggregation windows used by the billing rollup job were using local time arithmetic and naive interval rounding which produced short/long windows during DST boundaries. This caused some token-attribution ranges to be excluded while adjacent ranges were double counted, leading to negative adjustments and customer credit spikes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a tenant in a DST-aware timezone (e.g., Europe/Berlin).
2) Generate a mix of streaming and batched requests that span the DST boundary (e.g., 01:30 -> 03:30 on spring DST day).
3) Run billing rollup job that groups by local-hour windows using current code path (billing/rollup/service).
4) Observe overlapping or missing token attribution for sessions that straddle the clock change; invoices show negative lines during downstream normalization.
root_cause: The rollup logic computed per-hour windows by converting UTC timestamps into local time and then flooring to the hour using naive time arithmetic. During DST transitions window length changes (one hour becomes zero/ two hours depending on direction), and code relied on subsequent rounding that produced out-of-order half-open interval assignments. Additionally, session duration accounting mixed epoch_seconds with timezone-aware boundaries causing off-by-one-minute rounding at boundaries. The combination caused double-apportionment in one window and an omission in the adjacent window, and our invoice normalization step interpreted the omission as a negative correction instead of a carry-forward credit reconciliation.
mitigation: 1) Hotfix billing rollup to use UTC-anchored hourly windows (monotonic-based boundaries) and convert only for display. 2) Enforce half-open intervals [start, end) and canonical tie-breaker on session edge attribution. 3) Add an extra normalization pass that detects DST transition days and applies deterministic reallocation instead of negative line items. 4) Run targeted backfill for affected date ranges (see backfill plan).
deploy_notes: Deploy billing-service v2026.03.1 to staging, run full regression on DST transition test harness (see CI job billing-dst-check), then deploy to production during a maintenance window. Ensure SRE runbook is on-call for immediate rollback. Monitoring dashboards updated to show 'DST anomaly' metric and invoice deltas per-tenant.
rollback_plan: Revert PR and restart rollup workers. Run audit job to detect any invoices generated after revert and pause automated settlement until manual review completes.
backfill_plan: Backfill affected windows for tenants in DST zones between 2025-03-01 and 2026-03-31 with conservative re-aggregation. Job: jobs/billing_backfill_v2 with parameters tz=Europe/Berlin, date_range=2025-03-01:2026-03-31. Backfill will produce proposed credit adjustments and a reviewable diff; customer success will approve credits before applying. Expected runtime ~6 hours for top-200 tenants.
